In [[mathematics]], the '''Faber polynomials''' ''P''<sub>''m''</sub> of a [[Laurent series]]
:<math>\displaystyle f(z)=z^{-1}+a_0+a_1z+\cdots</math>
are the [[polynomial]]s such that
:<math>\displaystyle P_m(f)-z^{-m}</math>
vanishes at ''z'' = 0. They were introduced by {{harvs |txt |last=Faber |authorlink=Georg Faber |year1=1903 |year2=1919}} and studied by {{harvs|txt|last=Grunsky|authorlink=Helmut Grunsky|year=1939}} and {{harvs|txt|last=Schur|authorlink=Issai Schur|year=1945}}.
